thread.title: Intraday Update: Dow Gains 110 Points, but Bears Won’t Go Away Quietly

author: Brett Arends
title: Intraday Update: Dow Gains 110 Points, but Bears Won’t Go Away Quietly
text:
By Brett Arends May 14, 2018 1:20 p.m. ET Are stockholders getting tricked by a bait and switch?
Illustration: Bloomberg News Andy Lapthorne thinks so. The quantitative strategist at Societe Generale Securities warned clients Monday morning that although stock buybacks in the S&P 500 surged in the first quarter-- as highlighted on the cover of Barron's --it’s too soon to cheer the news, he says.
The total share counts fell by far, far less, he calculates.
The reason? Almost certainly, he says, because while companies are buying back stock with one hand, they are handing shares and options to top management with the other.
Quote: : “[Much] has been made, of the surge in repurchases, which leapt 20%+ in the last quarter as companies took advantage of repatriated cash and tax cuts to increase their buyback programs.”
(Though he also notes that “the S&P 500 is up over 20% over the last year so 20%+ is just keeping up with market prices”).
But, he warns, “it looks like the bulk of last quarter’s repurchases went on stock options (aka wages)…it appears as if buybacks have indeed gone to pay higher wages, but we suspect not in the way policymakers hand in mind.”
Illustration: Bloomberg News What a riot. Plus ça change , as the French say.
For good measure he adds that “When measured as a % of market capitalisation, businesses that buy back the most of their market cap underperformed – albeit not significantly so.”
Still, major market indexes edged up Monday. The president’s softer tone with China, noting he was sympathetic to job worries in the country, helped the mood. The S&P 500 (SPX) was up a few points, while (DJIA) gained just over a hundred. Among the most popular stocks, Netflix (NFLX) and Alphabet-Don't-Call-Me-Google (GOOG) were up nearly 1% by lunch. Apple (AAPL), Facebook (FB) and Amazon.com (AMZN) were marginally in the black.
Tesla (TSLA) fell nearly half a percent following reports a key executive has jumped to rival Waymo .
Crude oil jumped another half a dollar a barrel , breaking above $71 and threatening yet higher gasoline prices. And Treasury yields have resumed their ominous march higher, the 10-year yield rising 0.02 percentage points to 2.99%, just shy of the headline-worth 3%. The S&P is now well clear of its 200-day moving average, often seen as a useful indicator, but technical analyst Frank Cappelleri at Instinet warns it is now looking “overbought,” meaning it is vulnerable to a short-term pullback. “It overbought based on the short-term indicators I track, in particular the 14-Day Stochastic and the Bollinger Bands,” he tells me.
